title: Resveratrol Ameliorates Ethanol-Induced Acute Liver Injury in Mice and Primary Hepatocytes by Upregulating the AMPKalpha/Nrf2 Pathway.
authors: Zhang, Cuifeng; Cheng, Min; Lin, Weiqi; Zhang, Xiangyi; Yan, Jingjing; Xie, Xinyi; Xu, Qixiang; Chen, Qun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究白藜芦醇通过AMPKα/Nrf2通路改善乙醇性肝损伤，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is a major global health problem with few effective therapies. Resveratrol (RES) has demonstrated hepatoprotective effects, but its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We hypothesized that RES protects against ethanol-induced liver injury by activating the AMPKalpha/Nrf2 signaling pathway and upregulating downstream antioxidant enzymes. To test this hypothesis, a comprehensive approach was used, including in vivo and in vitro experiments, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. Using C57BL/6 mice and their primary hepatocytes, the therapeutic efficacy of RES in acute alcoholic liver injury. The results showed that RES markedly reduced liver histopathological damage and lessened ethanol-induced hepatocyte injury. These effects may be attributable to its antioxidant activity. RES increased AMPKalpha phosphorylation, as indicated by a higher p-AMPKalpha/AMPKalpha ratio, and promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation. Concurrently, RES upregulated mRNA and protein levels of heme oxygenase 1 (HO-1) and NADPH quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO-1). In primary hepatocytes from Nrf2-/- mice co-cultured with ethanol, HO-1 and NQO-1 levels remained largely unchanged, indicating a critical role for Nrf2 in RES action. Molecular docking studies suggested that RES binds effectively to AMPKalpha and kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1), with docking scores below -5 kcal/mol. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that the RES-Keap1 complex was highly stable, yielding a calculated binding free energy (Deltatotal) of -21.26 +/- 4.41 kcal/mol by MMPBSA analysis. In conclusion, RES improved hepatic function and reduced damage in ALD, potentially by modulating AMPKalpha, Nrf2, HO-1, and NQO1, and thus warrants further investigation for therapeutic application.
abstract_zh: 酒精性肝病（ALD）是一个重大的全球健康问题，目前有效疗法甚少。白藜芦醇（RES）已显示出保肝作用，但其分子机制尚未完全阐明。我们假设RES通过激活AMPKalpha/Nrf2信号通路并上调下游抗氧化酶来保护乙醇诱导的肝损伤。为验证此假设，采用了综合方法，包括体内和体外实验、分子对接及分子动力学模拟。利用C57BL/6小鼠及其原代肝细胞，评估了RES在急性酒精性肝损伤中的治疗效果。结果表明，RES显著减轻了肝脏组织病理学损伤，并减少了乙醇诱导的肝细胞损伤。这些效应可能归因于其抗氧化活性。RES增加了AMPKalpha磷酸化，表现为p-AMPKalpha/AMPKalpha比值升高，并促进了Nrf2核转位。同时，RES上调了血红素加氧酶1（HO-1）和NADPH醌氧化还原酶1（NQO-1）的mRNA和蛋白水平。在与乙醇共培养的Nrf2-/-小鼠原代肝细胞中，HO-1和NQO-1水平基本保持不变，表明Nrf2在RES作用中发挥关键作用。分子对接研究表明，RES能有效结合AMPKalpha和kelch样ECH相关蛋白1（Keap1），对接分数低于-5 kcal/mol。分子动力学模拟显示，RES-Keap1复合物高度稳定，通过MMPBSA分析计算出的结合自由能（Deltatotal）为-21.26 ± 4.41 kcal/mol。总之，RES通过可能调节AMPKalpha、Nrf2、HO-1和NQO1改善了ALD中的肝功能并减轻了损伤，因此值得进一步研究其治疗应用。
